out: Prison Link Cymru reports that 1,099 ex-offenders in 2015-16 struggled to find housing, with some living rough for up to a year. The Welsh Government acknowledges more people are receiving housing help, but changes to the Housing Act removed the right for prison leavers to priority accommodation. Andrew Stevens argues that building more one-bedroom flats is the best solution, estimating it would save the public purse significant funds compared to the cost of incarceration.

Police searched two city areas on Wednesday, recovering three firearms, ammunition, and a five-figure sum of money. A 26-year-old man was subsequently charged and appeared at Edinburgh Sheriff Court on Thursday.

Four young suspects, including Jordan Hill, Brittany Covington, Tesfaye Cooper, and Tanishia Covington, appeared in court charged with hate crimes, aggravated kidnapping, and battery against an 18-year-old white victim with schizophrenia. Prosecutors alleured the abuse occurred over several days, involving forced humiliation and forced consumption, while an online fundraiser has collected over $51,000 for the victim's mother.

Former Arsenal goalkeeper David Robinson has been appointed as the new director of football at West Brom. He played a key role in the Championship club's twice winning promotion to the Premier League in 2006 and 2012.

A "fasting-mimicking" diet, involving five days of low-calorie intake followed by 25 days of normal eating, reversed diabetes symptoms in mice by regenerating insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas. The diet appeared to trigger cellular reprogramming that restored pancreatic function, with benefits seen in both Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes models, though human trials showed similar effects. However, researchers caution against extreme dieting, emphasizing that the regimen mimics feast and famine cycles rather than serving as a quick fix.

Essilor and Luxottica are planning a merger to create a dominant player in the eyewear industry. The deal would generate significant synergies and innovation, benefiting customers but raising concerns about reduced choice and quality for consumers. If the merger goes through, the new entity, EssilorLuxottica, would become a "behemoth" of the industry, controlling almost everything offered to both independent retailers and chains.

Former Olympic silver medalist Emma Lloyd-Hughnow has accused British Cycling of "ageism" and "zero regard" for her welfare, joining other high-profile cyclists like Jess Varnish and Nicole Cooke in criticizing the program. The athlete revealed she felt "vindictated" by a leaked report detailing the organization's failures, which British Cycling has since admitted it did not pay "sufficient care and attention" to athlete wellbeing. In response, the governing body has implemented a 39-point action plan and apologized for past failings, as a government-commissioned

Kareem Badr turned a $20,000 investment in Austin's Hideout comedy club into a successful business by applying a "modular" approach to problem-solving, allowing him to quit his day job three years ago. The club has expanded to include a coffee house and theatre space, and Mr. Badr credits his computer science background to the club's growth. He notes that the venue is now positioned at "the right place at the right time," coinciding with a growing national enthusiasm for comedy, as industry data predicts a 1.8% annual revenue growth to

Ofcom abandoned plans to break up BT (British Telecom), citing "proodic reasons" such as the company's massive pension scheme and land-related complications. The regulator decided that separating BT's pension, which holds about £40 billion in assets and £10 billion in deficit, would be a costly hurdle, especially given the government's existing guarantee protecting the scheme BT fought to preserve in courts.

Branged Rodgers ahead of his second visit to Hampden with Celtic, he emphasized the importance of performance over luck as he aims to end his trophy drought. While reflecting on a previous defeat to Rangers, he stressed that focusing his own team's style of play is the key to success, insisting this tie is a priority despite the challenge of achieving a domestic treble.

Northern Ireland's universities face significant cuts, with Queen's University reducing undergraduate places by 1,010 over three years and cutting staff positions to offset an £8m subsidy reduction. The Education Minister warns these cuts may force students to study elsewhere, potentially damaging the local economy and the university's reputation.

The East Sussex NHS Trust confirmed that approximately 850 patients received incorrect appointment letters in March due to a printing company error, where a "two-week information leaflet" was mistakenly inserted into urgent cancer referral letters. The trust has apologized to those affected and emphasized that the mistake was an administrative error that could have caused unnecessary anxiety.

Labour is deeply divided over Brexit, with 47 MPs, including ten shadow ministers, rebelling against party orders to back the legislation last week. Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell has warned that frontbenchers who defy the whip could face dismissal, while Emily Thornberry insists the party will not "frustrate Brexit" despite the rebellion. The draft legislation returns to the Commons on Monday for three days of debate culminating in a vote on its third reading, with Labour attempting to amend the bill to secure a "meaningful vote" on the final deal.

The National League sold Republic of Ireland midfielder O'Kane to the Cherries for £175,000 in 2012, including a 15% sell-on clause. Manager Nicholson expressed frustration that he will not receive any of the transfer fee to help the "cash-strapped" club. The Gulls are still searching for new ownership after being forced to close their academy and reduce their playing budget following the departure of former owner Thea Bristow.

Iwan Wyn Lewis, a 36-year-old patient at Ysbyty Gwynedd, was found deceased in the Menai Strait in May. During an inquest, consultant psychiatrist Dr Olufemi Adebaba testified that a police visit to his ward "extremely unhappy" him and likely contributed to his agitation and distress, despite staff having ignored his request for extra medication the day before his death. The coroner is investigating whether the police interaction without special permission added to his mental state.

The 33-year-old has featured only twice for the Foxes this term, having signed a new one-year deal with the Premier League newcomers in the summer. Former Blackpool forward Taylor-Fletcher scored three goals in 23 games for his parent club last season. He joined the 13th-placed Owls prior to Saturday's Championship game against Norwich City.

Scientists are rushing to copy government data into private servers, fearing the Trump administration will restrict access to climate research. Dr. Waleed Abdalati warns this could represent a "tremendous paradigm shift" that harms taxpayers, while Prof. Robert Paterson compares the situation to the George W. Bush era, urging researchers to preemptively mirror data to avoid loss.

The Specials announced the death of founding drummer Bradbury, who passed away in England; his family and bandmates marked him as a pivotal figure in the ska and reggae scene. The news follows the recent passing of the band's trombone player, Rico Rodriguez, marking a significant loss for the group's legacy.

The 14-time major champion missed the cut at the Farmers Insurance Open after carding a level-par 72 in his second round, following an opening 76. World number one Jason Day and US Open champion Dustin Johnson also missed the cut at Torrey Pines. Overnight leader Rose carded a one-under 71 to put him on eight under.

Former Manchester United forward Cole suffers from kidney failure and is currently unable to participate in the Manchester United legends game against Barcelona due to medical restrictions. Having recently recovered from surgery and received a kidney transplant from his nephew, Cole is eager to return to playing, though he acknowledges he still has a "long road" ahead of him physically. He also believes the current gap between the English clubs and European powerhouses like Real Madrid, Barcelona, and Bayern Munich makes a Premier League title unlikely.

Pakistan has lifted its long-standing ban on YouTube after the video platform launched a country-specific version, allowing the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority to filter offending content directly. However, free access to the site remains active, though the government and activists have raised concerns about the transparency of the deal with Google. The ban, originally imposed in 2012 over the "Innocence of Muslims" film, is now lifted as Google expands its local versions to over 20 countries.

Leicester Tigers scrum-half Ben Benjamin is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the season after sustaining an injury during their recent win over Exeter. Director of rugby Richard Cockerill stated the 26-year-old will likely be unavailable for the final eight weeks of the campaign. Meanwhile, scrum-half Sam Harrison has signed a new contract, though the length of the deal remains undisclosed.

Doull Thomas helped Great Britain win the men's team pursuit gold in a world record time, securing Wales' seventh Olympic cycling gold and ending a 36-year medal drought. The 23-year-old, who previously won silver at the World Championships, described the victory as "surreal" and "drelike," joining teammates Wiggins, Burke, and Clancy to beat the world champions by 0.83 seconds. The win also saw Wiggins become the first Britishon to claim eight Olympic medals, capping a successful campaign for the team.

The death toll doubled over the last two days as officials recovered over 100 bodies from receding waters. Officials estimate the floods have affected 450,000 people in the state, with the monsoon affecting millions across at least 20 states. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is due to visit Assam on Tuesday to find a "permanent solution" to the yearly flooding.

A couple married at a Scottish ski resort, trading their traditional vows for a ceremony on the slopes. Bridget and Jonathan Reid tied the knot at Nevis Range, celebrating their shared passion for skiing that began six years ago. The intimate "ski" wedding, officiated by a Humanist Society member, featured the pair in full bridal attire gliding down the mountain as their first descent as husband and wife.

The Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) fined RBS $50 million for failing to prevent fraud by former trader Shirlina Tsang, who falsified emerging markets trade records. The penalty was reduced due to the bank's swift cooperation with regulators after discovering the illegal activity in 2011. This fine follows previous sanctions from the European Commission and US regulators totaling over $391 million for other compliance failures.

Backstage at the Baftas, Emma Stone joked that Mia Dolan "could ever win a Bafta or Oscar" before delivering a verdict of "Hopefully!" Tom Holland, the Rising Star winner, quipped that his legs were "in bits" from Spider-Man stunts, while Viola Davis passionately defended Meryl Streep against criticism, calling her "the most honourable, accessible human being you could possibly meet." Casey Affleck praised Meryl's Golden Globes speech, and Dev Patel confessed he was "a little bit wobbly" after his emotional Lion win

Murray's struggles this season have raised concerns about his fitness, with straight-set defeats to lower-ranked opponents like Jordan Thompson and Fabio Fognini. While he remains a dangerous conter for Wimbledon, his declining serve statistics and physical issues suggest he may not be fully fit to challenge for the title.

Mandla Hlatshwayo was shot after confronting a group of men who had robbed women of their phones in a pub. The suspects were found with drugs and an unlicensed firearm, and police are currently questioning them regarding the incident. The 40-year-old victim, who was also a local radio DJ, has been remembered as a selfless man as South Africa mourns one of its highest murder rates.

Witnesses reported hearing a gun being fired near Anfield Road Primary School around 09:00 GMT, prompting a lockdown at the school and the nearby All Saints Catholic Primary School. Merseyside Police are conducting house-to-house inquiries and reviewing CCTV footage to locate a dark-colored car driven by a white man, while school leaders confirm that pupils remain safe and the school day continues normally.

On Sunday, Ennis-Hill finished third overall after the first day of the heptathlon with 3,928 points, though she struggled in the long jump and javelin. With the 800m remaining, she sits on 5,544 points, still needing 6,200 to qualify for the Rio Olympics. A top-12 finish and a score of 6,075 would also secure her spot at this summer's World Championships.

Just Racing Services, the operating company for Manor, has gone into administration, effectively ending the team's participation in Formula 1. The collapse leaves 10 teams and 20 cars on the grid, coming shortly after the sport was acquired by US company Liberty Media. The collapse is attributed to financial instability and the loss of prize money, marking the end of an team that had existed since 2010.

The upcoming election on 2 March features 228 candidates, with 70 women and 22 independents. The DUP is fielding the most candidates (38), while the Workers Party and People Before Profit have the fewest. Newry and Armagh has the smallest number of candidates (nine), whereas West Tyrone, East Londonderry, and East Antrim have the largest (fifteen each).

The article addresses a reader's question about whether to exchange money now or wait for a December trip to New York. Anthony Reuben explains that the pound's recent decline against the dollar is largely due to differing economic out out between the US and UK, but notes that political events like the US presidential election in November could significantly alter exchange rates. He advises avoiding last-minute airport exchanges and using comparison sites to get better rates.

More than 300 people entered the Alternative Model of the Year competition, where Zoe Waters, a 19-year-old Newcastle University student, was crowned the winner. Ms. Waters stated she was "shoked" to be declared the victor, explaining that she has always dressed "how she wanted to look rather than following fashion." Organiser Kieran Martin emphasized the event was created to celebrate "different lives we have" and challenge prejudice against subcultures.

The Yomper statue, a memorial to the 1982 conflict, is currently at Eastney but faces a proposed move to Portsmouth Historic Dockyard as part of a £13m lottery-funded project. Campaigners and local officials insist the statue "belongs" at its current Eastney location, arguing it serves as a local Falklands War memorial that would lose its meaning indoors. The National Museum of the Royal Navy (NMRN) plans to relocate the statue to attract more visitors, though the director acknowledges it was "built for here [Eastney]" while consultations continue

A British citizen identified only as "BM" appeared at the Old Bailey accused of breaching Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim) orders twice in January. The Home Office refused to comment on the case, while the police stated they would prosecute where viable. The defendant was granted unconditional bail but remains subject to his TPim restrictions as the court heard he failed to contact a monitoring company and report to a police station on specific dates.

Seamer Anyon has been appointed as the new Sussex Cricket Academy director, taking over from Charlotte Burton. He will also coach the women's under-19 and under-21 sides. Additionally, Alexia Walker will assume roles with the senior, under-21 and under-19 sides.

Sunderland's 23-year-old younger brother, Wes Brown, is available for Bury's League One opener after a trial spell with the Shakers. The versatile defender has previously featured for Bradford, Doncaster, Oldham, Coventry, Ipswich, Watford, and Carlisle, accumulating over 50 Football League appearances. He is set to make his Bury debut in their Saturday trip to Doncaster.

The latest *Cinderella* adaptation, directed by Sir Kenneth Branagh, has dominated the US box office, earning $70m despite being a "completely faithful" reting to the 1950 classic. Lily James stars as the titular heroess, who Branagh defends as making "very clear" choices over her fate, contrasting with traditional "dreaming of the prince" tropes. While critics lament the film's "preserved-in-amber romanticism," the cast—including Helena Bonham Carter as the Fairy Godmother—seems to have won audiences

Ukraine banned Russian singer Julia Samoilova from the Eurovision contest due to a law prohibiting entry to Crimea, which Russia annexed in 2014. The ban sparked a diplomatic dispute, with Russia condemning the exclusion as political discrimination, while the European Broadcasting Union allowed Russia to participate via satellite from Moscow.

In 1961, a 16-year-old Alex McKechnie witnessed The Beatles perform at the Cavern Club in Liverpool, noting their unique, rebellious stage presence and musical adventiveness. He recalls the band's tight harmonies and defiant stage antics, which captivated a small, enthusiastic crowd and distinguished them from the era's cover bands. McKechnie would later become a regular attendee, deeply impacted by their raw energy and "reb" status.

South Africa is moving toward implementing a national minimum wage, with the deputy president Cyril Ramaphosa announcing that the country is "a step closer to finalising discussions." The proposed rate, recommended by an advisory panel, is currently about 47% of the wage needed to sustain a typical working-class household, though critics argue it is too low and could increase unemployment. While the government aims to introduce the wage within two years, labor unions and political parties remain divided on whether the measure will effectively combat poverty without hurting job growth.

Concern is mounting over a power struggle in Addis Ababa, which could trigger a regional chain reaction given Somalia's incomplete transition and tensions between South Sudan and Sudan. Meles Zenawi is remembered as a complex, transformative leader who modernized Ethiopia's economy and infrastructure but whose legacy remains contested due to stalled political reform and persistent poverty. He is viewed as an indispensable strategist who, despite autocratic tendencies and a patchy human rights record, fundamentally shaped the Horn's political landscape.

Australia secured a 39-run victory over Pakistan in the first Test, thanks to Jackson Bird's two-wicket haul. Azhar's half-century marked his 1,000th Test run, but play was halted by rain after tea, leaving the match's result unconputed.

In a Leith Walk by-election, the SNP's John Lewis Ritchie won the first seat with a 7.6% swing from Labour, while Labour's Marion Donaldson secured the second seat after transfers. The SNP also retained the Midlothian West seat with a 6.3% swing, as Kelly Parry defeated Labour's Ian Miller. Both by-election results saw the SNP hold ground against Labour, despite a low turnout of 25.1%.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that Russian air forces would continue supporting Syrian armed forces, urging Washington to separate moderate opposition from "terrorists." US Secretary of State John Kerry warned the US was "on the verge" of suspending talks, calling the situation "irrational" and lacking "notion or indication of seriousness." The US and Russia have been negotiating to secure a cessation of hostilities, but the latest truce collapsed after attacks on eastern Aleppo intensified, with 250,000 people trapped under siege.

Hooker Hughes and 19-year-old flanker Evans have been selected in Wales' squad for the upcoming Junior World Championship in Manchester. Both players enjoyed successful Six Nations campaigns and will face Ireland, Georgia, and New Zealand in Pool A. Scarlets' general manager Jon Daniels noted that the pair will enter the tournament with strong confidence.

Russia is furious over new U.S. sanctions, viewing them as politically motivated interference. The Kremlin, led by Dmitry Meddev and Zakharova, claims the outgoing Obama administration is scapegoating to sabotage relations before Trump takes office, while the U.S. State Department cites Russian intelligence harassment and election interference as justification.

Labury proposes abolishing university tuition fees and reintroducing maintenance grants, framing it as a fundamental principle of free education. The party costs the policy at £11.2bn annually, funded by tax changes, though the Institute for Fiscal Studies estimates a lower cost of £7.5bn to £8bn when accounting for loan write-offs. The move represents a stark policy choice, aiming to remove financial barriers to university access, though universities warn it may limit expansion due to government funding constraints.

An 11-person air show at Shoreham turned tragic when a Hawker Hunter jet crashed onto the A27 on August 22nd, killing 11 and injuring others. Sussex Police and Fire services have finished their scene work, but investigations continue as the Air Accidents Investigation Branch seeks to interview the pilot's family. Reopening of the closed lane is expected next week, though roadside screens will remain for land reclamation.

Dan Coats and Admiral Mike Rogers refused to discuss their conversations with President Trump regarding the Russia investigation during a Senate hearing, citing the need to protect such information. Their testimony largely failed to provide new details, frustrating senators who repeatedly pressed the officials on the probe. The hearing was seen as a "big letdown" compared to former FBI Director James Comey's upcoming testimony, who faces no current restrictions on discussing his interactions with the president.

A private party was held on Saturday, with a guest list of 500 including lobbyists, CEOs, and celebrities like Tyler Perry and Angela Bassett. The civil rights activist Al Sharpton tweeted about a performance by Prince and Steve Wonder, calling it "awesome". However, White Press Secretary Josh Earnest confirmed the Obamas paid for the event but declined to reveal the cost.

A series of road closures have been implemented across Northern Ireland, affecting routes in Loughgall, Poyntzpass, Dundonald, Hillsborough, Rathfriland, and Derrygonnelly. The specific closures include Causanagh Road, Tannyoky Road, Carrowreagh Road, Edenticullo Road, New Line Road, and Drumanure Road.

Emma Gleeson, a 34-year-old woman struggling with long-term anxiety and panic attacks, found that dietary changes significantly improved her mental health. After working with Dr. Rangan, she shifted to a diet of fresh, whole foods, reducing sugar and processed items, which led to fewer panic attacks, improved mood, and greater stress resilience. This highlights the growing evidence that nutrition plays a pivotal role in mental health, though it remains underutilized in standard medical practice despite the proven benefits.

The Alabama Securities Commission investigated author Harper Lee to determine if she was manipulated into publishing a decades-old manuscript. The commission closed the case, concluding she was capable of answering questions satisfactorily, while The New York Times noted the probe was sparked by a doctor's request. Lee's lawyer stated she was "extremely hurt" by the allegations of manipulation, despite the book's commercial success following the release of "To Kill a Mockingbird" in 1960.

The U.S. suspended bilateral talks with Russia over the collapse of the ceasefire in Syria, blaming Moscow and the Assad regime for intensifying attacks on civilians in Aleppo. Russia regretted the U.S. move, accusing Washington of failing to meet humanitarian commitments and shift blame for the truce's failure. The U.S. also halted cooperation on joint air strikes against jihadist groups, citing Russia's failure to protect aid convoys and Syrian regime adherence to the agreement.

Sha Khan's victory in the London mayoral election has sparked global celebrations, marking him as the city's first Muslim mayor. International leaders and media outlets hailed the win as a triumph over Islamophobia and a sign of London's growing liberalism. However, the result was overshadowed by the victory of Zac Goldsmith, who was criticized for his privileged background, and warnings about the rise of right-wing politics across Europe.

Parishioners at St Paul's in Shipley created a humorous job advertisement for a new vicar, which went viral after failing to attract applicants through a traditional advert. The role was ultimately filled by Henriette Howarth, who was selected based on criteria written by the children, including a love for Harry Potter and a commitment to keeping the church tidy. The initiative gained significant media attention, amassing over 30,000 views and highlighting the community's creative approach to filling the position.

Belgium international Koen De Bruyne suffered a significant leg injury during Everton's Europa League League Cup last-16 tie, initially ruled out for six weeks but later diagnosed as a 10-week absence. The injury threatens to miss up to 13 league and cup games, including the League Cup final. Despite this setback, De Bruyne expressed his determination to recover and return to playing football.

A 27-year-old Swiss man attacked passengers on a train in Selsetft, stabbing several and setting the vehicle ablight before being shot dead by police. The incident, which is currently being treated as not having a political or terrorist motive, left five people injured, including a six-year-old child in serious condition.

A Flybe passenger jet narrowly avoided a drone while flying at 900ft near Cornwall Airport Newquay on Tuesday. Police and aviation authorities are appealing for information to identify the reckless operator, as the incident highlights a complete disregard for public safety. The UK Civil Aviation Authority and Airprox Board are investigating the breach, which occurred as the aircraft approached for landing with 62 passengers on board.

A grey seal was found tangled in fishing nets at Cruden Bay, and the Scottish SPCA rescued and released it after removing the entnight. Chief Inspector John Carle described the seal as exceptionally large, requiring three officers to lift it, and warned that without intervention, the netting would have caused severe skin damage. The team was relieved the animal recovered quickly and was successfully returned to the water.

The National Library of Scotland has catalogued the archive of Sir Patrick Leigh Fermor, a war hero and travel writer, which includes letters from notable figures like Prince Charles and Truman Capote. The collection, spanning 16 metres of shelving, features his only surviving notebook from a 1933 European trek that inspired his most famous works. The library is digitizing the archive and plans exhibitions, noting that the collection was donated by the John R Murray Charitable Trust.

Mr Roache, the Yorkshire region secretary, won the general secretary election with 56.7% of the vote, defeating Paul McCarthy. He brings 35 years of experience and previously led a historic strike. In his role, Mr. Roache pledged to lead a "21st Century union" fighting for members and communities, paying tribute to outgoing general secretary Paul Kenny.

The singer discusses her upcoming second album and her nervousness about live TV appearances, admitting she struggles with stage fright and anxiety. She describes the "hellish" feeling of performing live, yet expresses genuine excitement and respect for Jools Holland, who she considers a "genuine champion" in the music world. Despite her fears, she is preparing for the broadcast by rehearsing new, darker tracks like "Phenomenal Woman" and "Kiss My Feet," aiming to captivate the audience with a visual album experience.

Jonas Gutiérrez revealed he was diagnosed with cancer last year, underwent surgery and chemotherapy, and made a emotional return to Newcastle United as a substitute in a defeat to Manchester United. He expressed his determination to prove he can still be a Premier League player while focusing on his recovery and future at the club.

Exeter City reported a record profit of £1.642m for 2014-15, primarily driven by the sale of Matt Grimes to Swansea City for £1.75m in January. The financial success came despite the club having to secure an emergency loan to pay player wages earlier in the year. The club also revealed a significant improvement in their financial base, reducing costs by almost 5% and moving from a shareholders' deficit to a surplus of £761,000.

A UAE athlete, Abdullah Hayayei, tragically died after the throwing cage collapsed on his head during training at the Newham Leisure Centre ahead of the World Para-athletics Championships in London. The incident, witnessed by his teammates, has sparked an investigation into health and safety protocols, with the IPC president confirming the team will compete in his memory. A moment of silence will be held during the championships' opening ceremony to honor the late competitor, who was preparing for F34 events including shot put, discus, and javelin.

The Scottish economy showed mixed growth at the end of last year, with manufacturers and tourism reporting positive trends, while retail and construction faced challenges from rising prices and skill shortages. Business optimism remains positive overall, but firms expect growth to be constrained by inflation, cash flow issues, and rising import costs throughout 2017.

The inquiry into undercover policing began at the Royal Courts of Justice, where Lord Pitchford stated it would likely expose both credible and discredutable conduct. The proceedings were prompted by allegations that officers formed relationships with women and fatherless children to gather information, with one victim, "Jacqui," describing the discovery of her partner's deception as "like an earthquake." The home secretary ordered the review following claims police spied on the family of Stephen Lawrence, and campaigners are demanding full disclosures to prevent further human rights abuses.

The All Blacks overcame a first-half deficit to defeat South Africa 19-12 in a gripping World Cup final. Despite trailing at half-time with a man down, New Zealand scored 12 unanswered points after the break, including a Beauden Barrett try, to secure victory and remain favorites to retain the Webb Ellis trophy. This was a physical encounter decided by a late drop-goal from Dan Carter, as the champions held a two-point lead for the last 12 minutes.

The Wellington monument on the Blackdown Hills is currently closed due to falling stone debris, prompting the National Trust to use ground-penetrating radar to inspect the 174ft tower's internal structure. The survey aims to identify voids in the stone cladding and establish a sustainable repair plan, as the landmark has a history of lightning strikes and requires renovation every 10 to 15 years.

Inditex, the world's biggest clothing retailer, reported an 8% increase in net earnings to €1.26bn, driven by an 11% sales jump to €10.5bn. The company emphasized its expansion into online markets, launching new payment systems and apps to connect its physical and digital stores, viewing online growth as a key strategy to offset slower physical expansion in Europe.

The Super Bowl halise show has evolved from a 12-minute sprint through hits into a high-studget political statement. Beyoncé’s 2016 performance, which leaned into black pride amid the Black Panthers-inspired visuals, set a new bar for activism, while Michael Jackson’s 1984 moonwalk became one of the most iconic—and surprising— moments, proving the event is no longer just a race for pure entertainment.

A new documentary, "The Betrayed Girls," airing on BBC One, revises the 2012 Rochdale grooming case, featuring victim Laura's account that abuse by Asian men remains ongoing. Former chief crown prosecutor Nazir Afzal highlights systemic failures, arguing victims are "not being consistently listened to" and agencies must collaborate more proactively to tackle the crime. Greater Manchester Police reiterate their commitment to tackling exploitation, emphasizing lessons have been learned and vital support for survivors.

A torrential flood at the Victoria Centre store caused a suspended ceiling to collapse and damaged stock, forcing the shop to close indefinitely. The closure was intended to allow for cleanup after water poured through a rooftop room, leaving the top floor under three inches of water. Staff are currently assisting with the cleanup as the store remains closed to recover from the damage.

A flood of automated comments was detected over the weekend, with more than 400,000 submissions using remarkably similar wording. Experts believe these bots are using stolen personal data to appear authentic, creating a "muddying of the waters" that could misrepresent genuine public opposition to the FCC's net neutrality proposals.

Sale Rugby chairman Steve Cotton has returned to the club to address declining attendances and outdated infrastructure at the AJ Bell Stadium. He aims to revitalize the "north of England" side by overhauling the board's involvement and improving the matchday experience for supporters. Cotton emphasized a collaborative approach with the coaching staff to ensure the club can compete at the highest level.

Moana debuted with an estimated $81.1 million, making it the second-highest Thanksgiving debut behind Disney's Frozen, but Disney withdrew a "brownface" costume after cultural appropriation allegations. Meanwhile, "Fantastic Beasts" led the US chart with $65.8 million, while "Allied" struggled with just $18 million amid Brad Pitt's marriage gossip, and "Rules Don't Apply" flopped with only $2.2 million.
The third seed secured a comfortable victory over an American wildcard in just over an hour, advancing to the last eight. She will face China's Saisai Zheng in the quarter-finals on Friday.
Two men were taken to hospital with injuries following an incident on Linn Road in the town on Sunday. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward with information about the attack.

Researchers investigating an Ebola outbreak in Guineaé traced the index case to Emile, a boy who played in a hollowed tree struck by fruit bats. The team found the tree had recently burned, causing a "rain of bats," and villagers had collected the insects for food. While bushmeat was ruled out as the source, scientists believe Emile’s exposure to bat droppings in the tree triggered the infection.

Mark Allen Bingham, the 39-year-old world number two, is considering his participation in the tournament based on whether his wife goes into labor before his first-round match against Joe Perry. He humorously suggested that if she delivers early, he would have to "hurry up" to play his shots quickly, but he and his wife need to discuss the timing before the event begins on Sunday.

The council voted to urgently remove a section of the pavilion to the seaward end due to the risk of further collapse. Work on the "dangerous" structure is expected to take about three weeks, with up to £650,000 set aside for the dismantling. Iwan Davies, the chief executive, emphasized that the dangerous nature of the structure makes the dismantling process inherently dangerous.

The £21.5m Castle Mill development at Port Meadow has faced significant criticism for its height and impact on Oxford's skyline and a protected scientific interest area. The Campaign to Protect Rural England is challenging the project at a High Court judge on 23 October, arguing that Oxford City Council failed to conduct an environmental impact assessment. Meanwhile, the University of Oxford intends to proceed with the development by October, asserting that mitigation measures are already in place.

The Olympus Trust, operating near Bristol, has warned parents of severe cuts due to government funding changes, describing the situation as "diabolic" and "terrible". A Department for Education spokesman said new plans would increase the trust's budget by 2.4%, but Mr. Baker warned that cuts could force the trust to shorten the school day, increase class sizes, and cut teaching and support staff. Parents are anxious about the impact, fearing that reduced funding will leave children with less pastoral care and support, while the government maintains the current system is "unfair" and "outdated".

A new study warns that designating forest reserves in Liberia and the Democratic Republic of Congo could displace up to 1.3 million people, as international funding aims to expand protected areas. Experts argue that displacing indigenous communities—who have lived in and protected these forests for centuries—is counterproductive, as their rights are often unrecognized despite their proven role in conservation. With funding from Norway and Germany, Liberia and DR Congo propose protecting 30% and 12-15% of their forests respectively, but analysts caution this risks violating local rights and causing violent conflict.

A human skull was discovered near a roundabout in Telford, prompting a police investigation. Authorities confirmed the remains are those of an adult male who had been at the location for at least two years. Forensic examinations are ongoing, and police are appealing to the public for information regarding missing persons as they work to determine the circumstances of the death.

At the 2024 Paris Olympics, Colombian boxer Yismar Dusmatov secured gold by winning a unanimous decision over two judges, while American Nico Hernandez and Cuban Joahnys Argilagos took bronze after semi-final losses. Meanwhile, 24-year-old Cuban Yusnisle Martinez became the first Olympic boxing finalist from Colombia.

University support staff unions are currently balloting on a 1.1% pay offer, which they have rejected as an "insult" given the significant salary cuts and vice-chancellors' pay rises. Strike action is possible in the autumn term if members feel they have no alternative, though the Universities and Colleges Employers Association maintains the offer is the "best available this year" and anticipates only "minor impact" on students.

The Scottish government has "called in" the proposal to close St Joseph's Primary School in Milngavie, citing concerns over "inaccurate information" in the council's consultation. East Dunbartonshire Council plans to merge St Joseph's with St Andrew's in a new Bearsden building, but the government's intervention means it will examine the process's validity. While the council argues the closures are necessary to modernize aging school estates and save budget money, parents and the Catholic Church oppose the plans, fearing they harm local education quality.

Kazu Miura, 49, has reignedited himself with the second division side past his birthday, extending his career over 30 years after starting in Brazil at 15. The prolific striker, who holds the record as Japanese football's oldest scorer, will continue to give "everything he has" despite previously opting out of a local cup competition at 49.

Security forces used tear gas against stone-throwing protesters in Indian-administered Kashmir, while seven people were reported killed in shelling across the Line of Control dividing India and Pakistan. The violence was sparked by the funeral of Burhan Wani, a militant leader killed last year, which led to restrictions and internet blackoffs in the region.

A "Leave" vote in the Brexit referendum was anticipated to cause significant financial market disturbances, prompting central banks to prepare contingency plans to ensure stability. The Bank of England and other global central banks stand ready to provide liquidity and intervene in currency markets, utilizing swap lines and foreign reserves to stabilize exchange rates and support bank borrowing if needed. While the Swiss National Bank has previously intervened to cap the franc's rise, the Bank of England is poised to act if sterling comes under pressure post-vote.

Former Sale prop forward Easter is retiring at 33 to pursue a teaching career at Wrekin College in Shropshire. Having joined Sale from Northampton in 2011, he enjoyed a decorated playing career but felt it was the right time to move on his own terms. He will play his final game for Sale at Newcastle on Saturday before transitioning into his new role.

Tawel Fan ward at Glan Clwyd Hospital was closed over three years ago following a report that some patients were treated "like animals," with families told their care may contributed to their deaths. The Betsi Cadwaladr health board acknowledged care quality could be a contributory factor, but a review of mortality rates remains unpublished despite being completed. An independent investigation is ongoing, with relatives receiving individual reports, though families remain unconceded lessons had been learned.

Declan Paul Butcher from Roe Park Court was sentenced to 14 months in prison for two separate assaults on Market Street in Limavady on October 2, 2014. CCTV footage showed him punching one victim unconscious and fracturing a second man's jaw. The judge cited the defendant's 51 previous convictions and "gratuitous violence" inflicted on "completely innocent" members of the public.

US Soccer midfielder Solo has been suspended from upcoming matches against France and England following a domestic violence charge that was later dismissed. The controversy stems from a DUI arrest involving her husband and a positive drug test from 2012, which Solo claims was an unknowing prescription error. In the midst of the scandal, Solo announced she is taking a break to "decompress" from the stress before returning to the team.

Three men—Omar Khan and two others—pleaded guilty to conspiracy to supply Class A drugs at Nottingham Crown Court. The case involved the recovery of 1kg of cocaine, and the defendants are due to be sentenced on 15 April.

British Transport Police have authorized the deployment of Tasers to officers, citing the "severe" terrorism threat and the need to protect the public. Specially trained officers will begin carrying the weapons over the next few weeks, with use subject to strict review following any discharge. The decision follows discussions with Police Scotland and briefings to Scottish Ministers, aiming to provide officers with an additional option to protect themselves or the public during genuine threats.

ID Systems, an industrial and commercial utilities company based in Glasgow, is expanding its workforce by creating new jobs in Glasgow and Lancashire. This growth is supported by a loan and equity investment from UKSE, the Tata Steel subsidiary, which will help fund the company's strategy and enable the creation of a new senior management team. The expansion follows ID Systems securing long-term projects, including off-site manufacturing for wastewater pumping stations, and the company aims to more than double its current staff of 80.

Helio Hermito Zampier Neto, a defender for Chapecoense, underwent surgery on multiple body parts and is reported to be in stable condition. The crash, which killed 71 people, saw five survivors, including the pilot who was warned about low fuel before taking off. Colombian and Bolivian authorities are investigating the crash, with evidence suggesting the plane ran out of fuel while en route to Medellin for a final match.

The 70-year-old Time Team presenter joined anti-tunnel campaigners to fight the plans, saying they placed the area's wider archaeology at risk. The protest by the Stonehenge Alliance was staged outside a consultation event in London earlier, where they argued that the proposed tunnel would damage the ancient landscape. Highways England maintains the scheme is necessary to reduce congestion and improve journey times, insisting it will help conserve the World Heritage Site despite opposition from heritage groups who demand longer, safer tunnels.

Everton took a 2-0 half-time lead through a Ricardo Rodriguez own goal and a Seamus Coleman header before Leighton Baines extended the advantage with a second-half penalty. Kevin Mirallas added a late fourth before Rodriguez grabbed a consolation with a curled free-kick, securing a 4-1 victory that puts Everton top of Group H.

The 35-year-old joined the Iron from Blackpool in 2013 and has made 119 league appearances for the League One side. He helped them to a third-placed finish this season, before they were beaten by Millwall in the play-off semi-finals. Bishop told the club website: "With the way the season finished, it's a sense of unfinished business and it was disappointing for all of us."

Pawel Sroka has been charged with the murder of his partner, Joanna Trojniak, following a post-mortem examination that confirmed she died from a chest stab wound. Sroka is due to appear at Bromley Magistrates' Court on 4 April while the victim's next of kin have been informed.

Researchers have identified 80 new genetic markers for prostate cancer through the COGES study, analyzing samples from over 200,000 people. The discovery of markers specifically linked to aggressive forms of the disease aims to facilitate the development of a viable screening test and improve future diagnosis and treatment. Professor Neil Burnet at Addenbrooke's Hospital is also working to improve radiotherapy targeting, seeking to reduce toxicity and better treat the disease in its earlier stages.

Worcester fought valorously but ultimately lost 24-19 to Wasps at home, with tries from Wade and Rowlands either side of Josh Adams' scores. The match saw Biyi Heem dismissed for a tackle on Le Roux, leaving the hosts with 14 men, though Dai Young's side secured a play-off spot as Warriors remain nine points clear of 10th-placed Sale.

French President Francois Hollande expressed "deep sadness" over the death of Huguette Dupeu, as most of the victims in the terrorist raid were foreign tourists. The attack, claimed by Islamic State, was the deadliest in Tunisia since the 2011 uprising that ousted Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali, leading to the dismissal of six police chiefs and the arrest of over 20 people in connection with the raid.

Strfor's analysis reveals that almost all structures at Mosul airport have been destroyed, rendering the runways unusable for attacking forces. The destruction, which includes sabotaged taxiways and aprons, is part of a broader offensive involving Iraqi security forces, Kurdish Peshmerga, and Sunni and Shia militiamen, backed by US-led coalition airstrikes, to reclaim the city from IS militants. The damage serves to clear lines of sight for IS defensive positions, though the airport's destruction is likely more difficult to repair than the Qayyarah air base, which was

Network Rail is carrying out major signalling improvements between Good Friday and Easter Monday to complete the Reading station redevelopment. The disruption is intended to allow the last major stage of work to be finished, with hundreds of buses on standby in case of overruns. On 27 December, King's Cross and Paddington were shut due to engineering works overrunning, and further closures are scheduled for the Easter break.

Plans were approved for Coastal Oil and Gas Limited to drill in a field at St Nicholas, though the permit does not allow hydraulic fracturing. Natural Resources Wales approved the exploratory drilling following a thorough assessment, requiring land reinishment within 12 months. The decision comes despite a temporary fracking ban in Wales and the Welsh Labour ministers' preference for renewable energy over the "unproven" technology.

Amazon has announced it will shift the registration of European sales from Luxembourg to local branches in the UK, Germany, Spain, and Italy, ending a long tax-avo avoidance practice. The move follows recent EU investigations into "il state aid" deals involving Amazon, Apple, and Starbucks. The change comes as the company begins establishing local branches in France and aims to comply with intensified EU scrutiny of global tax arrangements.

Junior doctors in England have begun strike action, with further walkouts planned in November, to protest pay and working conditions. The British Medical Association (BMA) argues that the current contract is outdated and undafir, threatening to impose a new deal next year despite ongoing negotiations. Dame Sally Davies warns that the strikes will lead to patients suffering, emphasizing the vital role of junior doctors in the NHS and the need to ensure they feel valued.

Oxford midfielder Kenny will be eligible to play against Barnsley in the Football League Trophy final on Sunday after impressing the coaching staff. Having joined the England Under-20 squad over Easter and made 13 appearances for the U's, head coach Michael Apppton praised his form, noting he is "highly thought of at Goodison Park and has a big future."

Kingston Maurward College near Dorchester received £3.24 million to build a new animal sciences facility, while Weymouth College was awarded £0.5 million to refurbish two buildings. These grants are part of a £214 million investment across 47 colleges in England, aimed at improving facilities to support skills training and employment in sectors like animal science.

Greg Dyke has invited Astle's widow and daughters to Wembley Stadium to discuss the risks of heading footballs, following the campaign by the family and "Justice for Jeff" group. The meeting comes after a neurosurgeon confirmed that the former West Bromwich Albion forward, Jeff Astle, died from a brain condition linked to heading heavy leather balls rather than Alzheimer's disease. Dawn Astle emphasized the seriousness of the issue, stating that once the brain is damaged, it cannot repair itself, and her father is proof of that.

The article discusses the growing wealth gap between the global elite and the rest of society, noting that a threshold of around $100 million is where serious wealth management begins. It highlights that while the world has become generally richer, the divide between the top 1% and everyone else has widened since the 2008 financial crisis. Furthermore, the piece features perspectives from figures like Robert Kuhn, who suggests the internet has made people more aware of wealth, but argues that increasing inequality is leading to hostility toward the very wealthy.

The 18-year-old identical twins have made nine Premiership appearances this season, featuring for both the club and England Under-20s. Director of rugby Steve Diamond praised their potential, noting they are the fourth pair of twins to play together in the league's top tier. Tom also marked his debut with a try in Sale's win over Bristol, becoming the club's youngest Premiership try scorer.

Police are appealing for witnesses after a man was seen near Corbett Place and Calais View in the early morning. The suspect is described as being in his late teens or early 20s, approximately 5ft 9in tall, with dark curly short hair and wearing a dark top.

The US, UK, and Canada blocked an Egypt-backed regional forum aimed at pressuring Israel to clarify its nuclear weapons status, citing unrealistic conditions. The failure of the talks means the next review is set for 2020 at the earliest.

The UK government is accelerating fracking development, prompting a letter from Natural Resources Minister Carl Sargeant to Welsh councils reminding them of the temporary ban in Wales. Energy Secretary Amber Rudd has instructed English councils to approve applications within 16 weeks to prevent delays. The Welsh government maintains its moratorium, prioritizing renewable energy over fossil fuel extraction.

Following Tyson's defeat, Fury dominated the heavyweight division, unified the belts, and sensationally dethroned Klitschko in Dusseldorf last November. However, his victory was immediately followed by a public struggle with mental health issues and a withdrawal from a scheduled rematch due to depression. Fury's subsequent reign has been mar by questions regarding his focus and commitment, with his camp alleging media agendas while he candidly discusses his ongoing battles with sanity and appetite.

Premiership boss Dai Young expects several in-form Wasps players to make Eddie Jones' England squad, with Nathan Hughes and Guy Thompson impressing. Meanwhile, Leicester's Will Evans is set to be named despite his director of rugby insisting he is "not ready for international rugby" yet. The final 35-man squad will be named on October 26 ahead of the autumn Tests.

The exhibition "From Dark to Light" at The Old Low Light Heritage Centre explores the life and work of Victor Noble Rainbird, a North Shields-born artist who lived from 1887 to 1936. It features his paintings of the North Sea and hometown streets, alongside previously unseen sketches from his active service in the Northumberland Fusiliers during World War I. Curator Dave Young emphasizes that this is the first major hometown exhibition of Rainbird's work, aiming to "shed new light" on the "much misunderstood" artist's remarkable legacy.

Former Celtic boss Gordon Strachan is set to benefit from Scott Brown's return, with Lennon stating the midfielder's decision would "boost" the Scotland squad for the World Cup qualifier against England. Lennon believes Brown, now 31, is revitalized and can be a key asset, insisting Scotland "can win" the Wembley clash despite the veteran's premature retirement. Mark McGhee added that Brown's leadership and influence would make other players better, suggesting his return is a positive boost for the national side.

A buzzard became trapped in a wire fence in Bethesda while chasing a wood pigeon. RSPCA Inspector Mike Pugh freed the bird, noting it had luckily avoided major feather damage before being released back into the wild.

The Communication Workers Union announced a walkout starting December 19, involving thousands of workers at Crown Post Offices during Christmas Eve. The Post Office maintains that operations will continue as "business as usual" with at least 97% of its 11,600 branches remaining open. Despite the strike, the union demands the management to pause closure plans and pension changes, while the Post Office has agreed to resume talks to address the dispute.

Ulster Unionist leader Mike Nesbitt opened his party's manifesto launch by declaring "Dominion doesn't work, partnership does," framing the election as a referendum on "incompetence, arrogance, cronyism and the strong whiff of corruption." He defended his recent comments about transferring votes to the SDLP, insisting he has "no regrets," while arguing that a nationalist party taking power is preferable to an SDLP or Sinn Féin coalition.

Irish police, customs, and the medicine watchdog seized over 60,000 vials containing anabolic steroids and human growth hormones during raids in Muff and Lifford. A man in his 30s was arrested but later released without charge, while authorities confirmed evidence of an illegal manufacturing operation.

Taoiseach Enda Kenny suggested that a border poll could be triggered if there was clear evidence of majority support for Irish unity, prompting unionist politicians to warn it was "mischievous" rhetoric. Meanwhile, unionist leaders argued the current priority was economic stability rather than constitutional polls.

Morecambe secured a 1-0 victory over Yeovil to claim the league's top spot, while also defeating Rotherham 5-4 in the EFL Cup. 40-year-old striker Kevin Ellison credited his professionalism and recovery for his continued success, with manager Ian Bentley praising his "desire" and "attitude towards training."

Qatar has rejected a 13-point list of demands from Saudi Arabia and its allies, including Egypt, the UAE, and Bahrain, which accuse the country of backing terrorism. The demands require Qatar to reduce ties with Iran, close a Turkish military base, and shut down Al Jazeera, among other conditions. Meanwhile, UUS Secretary of State Rex Tillerson said the proposals provided a basis for dialogue leading to a solution of the crisis.

Ms. Evans, currently suspended from UKIP, has abandoned her bid to become the next leader, claiming a "handful of people at the top" blocked her path despite a six-month ban for " bringing the party into disrepute." She is instead backing councillor Lisa Duffy, arguing UKIP needs a "clean break from the past" to move from being "just a rugby club on tour" to a serious political party. Despite losing a High Court bid to overturn her suspension, Ms. Evans maintains her "determined" support for the party, believing the right leader could make "

A 26-year-old woman was raped in a secluded area after using an Uber app to book a taxi in Delhi. The driver, Shiv Kumar Yadav, has been charged with criminal intimidation and confessed to the crime, leading to a ban of several web-based taxi firms by the police. The incident has renewed global outrage over sexual violence in India, though recent laws have failed to act as a deterrent.

Wales' historic Euro 2016 campaign ended in the semi-finals against Portugal, but the team and fans shared a mutual adoration that defined the tournament's spirit. Despite the loss, Wales' "Red Wall" of supporters celebrated a remarkable run that saw the nation qualify for a major tournament for the first time in 58 years, captening the hearts of the country with songs like "Don't Take Me Home" and a newfound belief in their team's ability to compete with Europe's elite. The bond between the players and fans was symbiotic, propelling the country

Renfrewshire remains the most deprived area in Scotland for the second consecutive time, with Glasgow and Edinburgh also featuring among the most deprived. The Scottish government and opposition parties agree that deep-rooted poverty and UK welfare cuts are sustaining these inequalities, despite recent local initiatives aimed at regeneration.

Cassells and Scrimgeour won the lightweight pairs title at the Rotterdam championships, clocking 6:29.63 to finish ahead of Denmark and China. The British duo retained the European title they claimed last year, while Ireland's Paul O'Donovan advanced to the semi-finals of the lightweight single sculls.

The 22-year-old Johnston has signed a one-year contract with the Scottish Championship club, joining fellow new signings Craig Barr and Mark Stewart. Having progressed through Kilmarnock's youth ranks, Johnston previously played 34 times for Kirkcaldy last season. Additionally, Barr and Stewart have also committed to the club, with the latter scoring five goals in 36 appearances last term.

Liverpool overcame a first-half deficit to defeat Swansea 2-1, with Leroy Fer opening the scoring before Roberto Firmino and Milner equalising and winning respectively. Despite the victory, Swansea remain in the relegation zone and manager Guidolin's job hangs in the balance amid a run of poor form.

The article highlights the shock of a positive steroid test in Scottish rugby and the frustration over qualification rules, while noting that drug testing in the sport remains low, with only around 1.4% of elite players testing positive, though the author suspects higher rates in lower leagues. The piece also questions the pressure on players to use supplements and steroids, suggesting the culture of weight training may be pushing athletes toward artificial aids despite the clear rules against doping.

TRNSMT, a new festival replacing the cancelled T in the Park, will open at Glasgow Green on August 14, featuring acts like Kasabian, Biffy Clyro, and The Kooks across three stages. The event faces tight security following recent terror attacks, with armed police patrolling the site and a zero-tolerance policy on drugs. Organised by DF Concerts, the festival aims to move past the " challenging two years" since T in the Park relocated, though highlights will be broadcast on a BBC Scotland programme.

North Korea has restarted operations at the Yongbyon nuclear reactor, declaring it ready to face U.S. hostility with nuclear weapons. The White House warns Pyongyang to focus on fulfilling international obligations rather than advancing its nuclear program. Experts remain skeptical of North Korea's capabilities, noting the program's unclear status despite previous provocations and stalled six-party talks.

Cambridgeshire Police reopened a murder inquiry into the disappearance of Andrew Bedford, 27, after discovering human remains at a garage in Ramsey. A 64-year-old man has been arrested, and detectives believe Bedford was shot with a shotgun at Mongrel Cars on the evening of September 28th. Authorities are conducting further forensic analysis, including DNA testing, while appealing for local witnesses to come forward.

Salford City Reds owner Dr. Marwan Koukash is aggressively attempting to transform the club into a Super League powerhouse within three to four years by lobbying to raise the salary cap and sign high-profile players like Adrian Morley and Sam Tomkins. Former coach Brian Noble has expressed enthusiasm for working with Koukash, believing the businessman's passion and financial backing could finally realize his dream of making Salford the biggest rugby club in the country. However, the article notes that while the ambition is clear, the "done deal" status remains uncertain, as similar discussions about available funds have seen

Ireland secured a 3-0 start in Bangkok as Isobel Joyce claimed 4-20 to dismiss Zimbabwe for 78. Clare Shillington and Cecilia Joyce then guided Ireland to 79-3 in 15.2 overs. Victory over Scotland will now secure Ireland a place in next year's World Twenty20.

Colchester Hospital was rated as inadequate following a Care Quality Commission inspection that found it was relying on "unsuitable" agency staff. Norman Betchley died in 2009 after an agency nurse mistakenly fed him a pill. The hospital's chief executive, Frank Sims, admitted the biggest challenge is reducing dependency on agency workers, acknowledging they still have "a long way to go" despite recent recruitment efforts.

Cavendish finished sixth in the scratch race and seventh in the elimination race, while Colombia's Fernando Gaviria Rendon won the individual pursuit. In the women's sprint, Becky James broke the Olympic record and advanced to the quarter-finals, alongside Katy Marchant, while France's Thomas Boudat leads the overall standings. The fourth event, the time trial, begins on Monday before the flying lap and points race events.

Finance Minister Máirtín Ó Muilleoir announced a reallocation of £200m to health services in the 2016/17 budget, bringing the total additional funding to the sector since last year's monitoring round. The money will be directed toward unscheduled care, emergency departments, and hospital bed blocking issues, though the Health Minister will finalize specific allocations in the coming days. Additionally, £30m was reallocated to schools and £25m to roads maintenance, with the Finance Minister noting no new spending cuts despite ongoing budget pressures.

The Winklevoss twins have refocused their legal battle against Facebook, filing a new lawsuit alleging the company suppressed evidence during their previous settlement. The dispute stems from the twins' original claim that Mark Zuckerberg stole their idea to create the social networking site, which formed the basis of the 2010 film "The Social Network." Despite reaching a financial settlement in 2008, the twins attempted to reopen the case in 2011 seeking more money, but a U appeals court ruled they must accept the original deal. In their latest suit filed this week

A teenage pedestrian was struck by a Ford Focus on Oldgate Lane in Threborough on Saturday; the driver was uninjured while the car was heading towards Dalton. Police are appealing for witnesses to contact them.

Harry Chapman Pincher, a Daily Express defence correspondent, was renowned for his uncapped ability to memorize minute details without taking notes. After retiring, he alleged that Britain's security services had been penetrated by spies at the top level. He cultivated a wide network of contacts, ranging from senior civil servants and politicians to the countryside, often gathering intelligence over lunch or while game shooting, and famously recounted that MI5 monitored his conversations but took no action.

Dester, who was in the final year of his contract at Dens Park, had scored six goals in three games for Dundee already this season. He could make his Blues debut in Saturday's Championship match at Leeds. Birmingham opened their Championship campaign with a goalless draw against Cardiff City and were knocked out of the EFL Cup by League One side Oxford United in Tuesday's first-round tie.

A former private in her 20s accepted a conditional caution for misconduct in a public office after agreeing to pay £40 to an armed forces charity. She was arrested in Nottinghamshire as part of Operation Elveden, which was originally investigating phone-hacking at the News of the World newspaper but was widened to include other public officials. The Crown Production Service decided against prosecution due to public interest considerations, with lawyer Gregor McGill stating the evidence was sufficient but a caution was the appropriate course of action.

The Care Inspectorate conducted unannounced inspections at Nithsdale House and Drumpellier Lodge in February, both receiving low ratings—one and two—across multiple categories. At Nithsdale House, the home was rated "unsatisfactory" for care quality, environment, and staffing, while Drumpellier Lodge was rated "weak" for failing to meet 10 previous improvement requirements. Inspectors noted "very little progress" at both sites, expressing ongoing concerns about resident wellbeing and medication administration.

Police were called to Derby Road, Enfield at 15:30 GMT on Saturday after reports of a gun being seen in a car. The vehicle was stopped at 16:00 GMT, and the four men inside were arrested and are currently being held at a north London police station.

A power outage affecting over 53,000 properties in Lancaster was caused by an unknown fault at the Caton Road substation, impacting travel, schools, and businesses. Power was fully restored by 16:30 BST, though the firm acknowledged the cause remained a mystery and thanked customers for their support during the disruption.

The High Court quashed Sajiv Javid's refusal to approve development at Hatchfield Farm, ruling his decision was "plainly deficient" and inconsistent with national planning policy. The judge ordered a reconsideration, emphasizing the need for more housing in the Forest Heath District. The case will now be reheared, with local parish councils arguing growth should be concentrated in Newmarket rather than dispersed across rural areas.

The council leader announced the Cowes crossing would be free until 2 July in recognition of the new vessel's issues, while the transport councillor confirmed compensation discussions were underway for damaged cars and businesses. The ferry has faced significant delays and operational failures since its late May launch, including groundings and electrical faults, prompting an auditor review and ramp extensions to resolve vehicle scraping.

Tilly Sliti has signed a three-year contract with Lille after joining on a season-long loan last summer. The 24-year-old Tunisia international has made just five appearances since the 2017 African Cup of Nations and has scored once in 16 games for the club. Lille sit 11th in the table ahead of their Saturday fixture against Metz.
British astronaut Tim Peake shared experiments and spoke with schoolchildren from space, where he has been stationed for six weeks.

Martyn Irvine made history by becoming the first Irish cyclist to win a world track title in 117 years, adding a silver medal at the World Championships in Belarus. He also secured a World Cup gold in Manchester and an European bronze before being crowned as BBC Northern Ireland's Sports Personality of the Year, overcoming a serious injury to claim the accol ahead of rivals like AP McCoy.

A major emergency was declared at Prestwick Airport after an Italian C-27J aircraft lost communication. The plane was escorted by RAF Typhoons to the airport and landed safely shortly before 20:00. While Scottish airspace was not closed, flights at Glasgow and Edinburgh experienced short delays, and the incident was resolved without further disruption.

West Midlands Counter Terrorism Unit officers arrested five men in Stoke-on-Trent and Birmingham on suspicion of terrorism-related offenses following the discovery of suspect devices in Lee Bank. Police have been granted additional detention time as investigations continue, with nearby roads cordoned off and properties searched across the West Midlands.

The tournament begins on Friday, 10 June, with the final at the Stade de France in Paris on 10 July. Spain are hoping to retain the title they won in 2008 and 2012, while England appear at their ninth finals after Wales and Northern Ireland qualified for the first time. With 24 teams in the finals and a group-stage knockout format, only the top two and four best third-placed finishers will qualify for the last 16.

Great Britain will face Greece in a warm-up game at the Copper Box in London on Sunday, with the match starting at 5:30 PM BST and stream live on BBC iPlayer and the Sport website. The contest serves as a final preparation for Great Britain's EuroBasket campaign, where they will be missing three key team members but will look for revenge against the European title contenders.

Wales suffered an 11th consecutive defeat against Australia, failing to convert their numerical advantage despite a strong defensive effort. Despite Dan Biggar's kicking efforts, Wales were repelled by Australia's extraordinary defense, notably Taulupe Faletau's dropped ball and George North's try-line hold-up. Australia now face Scotland in the quarter-final, while Wales' path forward remains fraught with frustration despite a courageous rearguard action.

Scotland coach Gregor Townsend will take over from Kenny Cotter at the end of the season, while Strauss expects a high-intensity send-off for the Ireland match. Ireland, having won 14 of their last 17 Six Nations fixtures and dominated set-piece specialists like South Africa and New Zealand, enter as strong favorites despite Scotland's eager desire to give Cotter a "good send off."

Retired General Petraeus warns that "industrial-strength" extremists cannot be defeated by military force alone, emphasizing the need for political strategy and Sunni support. He views the recent loss of Ramadi as a "strategic loss" for IS, believing the group will likely be retaken soon but acknowledging it represents a significant setback requiring augmented efforts. He argues that success depends on political change, specifically incentivizing Sunni Arabs to support the new Iraq rather than oppose it.

A cyberattack on the City of Edinburgh Council's website service provider, based in England, occurred 10 days ago. Officials have reassured the public that only email addresses were accessed and confirmed no other personal details were compromised. Extra security measures have been implemented, and the incident has been reported to the Information Commissioner and the UK Government's Computer Emergency Response Team, and affected individuals are being contacted for support.

A joint operations room was formed by rebels in response to increased attacks on residential areas and displaced people. The cessation of hostilities brokered by the US and Russia has seen a significant reduction in violence, but escalating fighting around Aleppo threatens to push peace talks toward collapse. The Syrian opposition delegation in Geneva intends to suspend formal participation, accusing the UN of bias after proposals regarding President Assad's role were floated.

Instagram is planning to introduce ads in the coming months to transition into a sustainable business, following its acquisition by Facebook for $1 billion. The initiative comes as the platform, which has 150 million users, seeks to monetize its popularity after previous attempts to sell user photos were rejected by the community; the company emphasized that "As always, you own your own photos and videos." Early efforts by Instagram to generate revenue were met with user backlash, such as when the company changed the terms of service to seemingly indicate that it would own user images and could sell those images to advertisers

The 2016 Mercury Music Prize shortens its long list of 12 nominees down to six finalists, with a public vote deciding the winner alongside a panel of judges. The shortlist includes acts like Hot Level, Radiohead, and the late David Bowie, whose Lazarus track is widely interpreted as a personal epitheg. The ceremony takes place at Hammersmith Apollo on September 15th and will be broadcast live on BBC Four.

Gurpal Virdi, a 56-year-old former Metropolitan Police officer from Hounslow, was acquitted of indecent assault and misconduct in a public office at Southwark Crown Court. The retired detective claimed the case was part of a 17-year police campaign to "hunt" him out of the force, alleging they targeted him after he reported racism within the ranks. The charges dated back to November 1986, and Virdi retired from the force in 2012 after 30 years of service.

The UK government is under pressure to change its approach to leaving the EU, which critics call a "hard Brexit." Mr. Cairns' predecessor, Stephen Crabb, claimed the election had changed the terms of the Brexit debate, arguing that the UK should stay in the single market and customs union while still leaving the EU legally. Mr. Cairns is backing calls for Theresa May to adopt a more flexible approach to achieve cross-party consensus, emphasizing that remaining in the single market is "completely wrong" given the opposition of the two largest parties.

Hillsborough families met with Home Secretary Theresa May to discuss the aftermath of the inquiry, which concluded in April and ruled the fans unlawfully killed. The talks focused on police conduct and the potential for criminal prosecutions, with May pledging to ensure the "Hillsborough Law" would place a further onus on those in public office to cooperate with investigations. The families welcomed the jury's findings but face continued uncertainty as they await decisions from the Crown Prosecution Service on whether any individuals should be charged.

The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has issued new guidance stating that online harassment and "virtual mobbing" can lead to prosecution, treating internet offenses with the same severity as offline crimes. However, the director emphasized that this is not an attack on free speech but will focus on context and severity. The guidance specifically targets "doxing" and aims to help police identify online crimes more easily.

Despite this, a campaigner with autism highlighted that current laws often fail to protect victims of transphobic abuse, especially when perpetrators operate from abroad, leaving many victims with "no escape

Faizan, a young boy, was killed during protests near a polling station in Srinagar. Witnesses report he was shot in the back of the head while trying to understand the commotion, and he died before receiving medical care. His death is part of a broader day of violence in which paramilitary forces fired on protesters, resulting in eight fatalities and a historically low voter turnout of 7.1%.

North Wales Police were called to a serious incident involving a Ford Transit truck on Nantlle Road in Talysarn, Gwynedd, on Friday afternoon. A woman was airlifted to Ysbyty Gwynedd in Bangor but later died from her injuries. Police are currently appealing for witnesses to the crash.

Four bidders—Abellio, Arriva, KeostiAmey, and MTR—have submitted proposals for the next Wales and Borders rail franchise. The successful bidder will be required to reinvest profits into the railway and deliver major upgrades to the Cardiff Metro scheme. A contract is slated to be awarded in early 2018, with the Welsh Government focusing on service quality and passenger numbers.

80-year-old broadcasting legend Robbie has stepped down from his long-running show "Take the Floor" after 35 years on BBC Scotland. Known for championing Scottish traditional music and culture, he is passing the batel to younger presenter Gary Innes, with First Minister Nicola Sturgeon wishing him well.

Carlisle United have had three home games postponed due to flooding at Brunton Park, with their recent match at Preston's Deepdale being played as scheduled. Manager Alan Coleman criticized the league's handling of the situation, arguing that it creates an "unfair advantage" for his team while other sides face an disrupted schedule. The Cumbrians will now face upcoming fixtures at Blackburn's Ewood Park and Blackpool's Bloomfield Road.

Two Manchester United supporters were found on the pitch before the Arsenal game on Saturday and handed over to police, who decided not to arrest them. The pair had been on a stadium tour and were searched before the incident, which comes six months after a false explosive was found at Old Trafford. United confirmed there was no risk to supporters attending the game, and the incident is believed to be linked to a training exercise.

Accrington Stanley secured a 3-2 victory over Preston North End in extra time, with Billy Kee scoring the decisive goal in the third minute of stoppage time. The match was level at 2-2 after extra time before Kee's winner. Preston had numerous chances but were ultimately punished by Accrington's set-piece efficiency.

Andrew Bickel, a 39-year-old man, experienced a viral social media maccap after he mistakenly left his tools at a Catwel shop, only to have a woman from the Cat Charity shop call him to say they were there to collect. He enjoyed the sudden fame, turned down TV appearances, and joked about donating money to animal charities if the story continued to grow.

Muir, a 24-year-old middle-distance runner, will miss the Commonwealth Games in April due to a conflict with her university exams, despite finishing fourth and sixth in the 1500m and 5,000m at the World Athletics Championships. She expressed disappointment but emphasized that completing her degree remains "really important" to her, stating she is "gutted" to be missing the event.
