Former Newcastle striker Nile Ranger has been jailed for eight months after admitting online banking fraud, which has delayed his pre-season training with League One side Southend. Manager Phil Brown expects Ranger to return to training before the first league game on August 5, but acknowledges the player needs to regain match fitness after his recent legal issues. Ranger, who joined Southend in 2016 and scored eight goals last season, will likely need a week's work to be fit for the start of the campaign.

Veteran broadcaster Sir Terry Weldy died of cancer at 77, leaving behind a legacy of five decades in broadcasting. His family and colleagues, including BBC Radio 2 host Ken Evans, paid tribute to him as "radio's absolute governor" and a beloved figure who "made the world laugh."

Unions at BAE Systems have warned of possible delays to funding for the Royal Navy's new frigates, but Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson insisted there was no change to the timetable. Labour and the Lib Dems called for an end to uncertainty, while the UK government confirmed in its Strategic Defence and Security Review last November that eight Type 26 frigates would be built on the Clyde, though the total number was scaled back from 13.

The Republican presidential candidates Marco Rubio and Ted Cruz intensified their attacks on frontrunner Donald Trump, targeting his business record and conservative credentials, while Trump retaliated with sharp personal insults. With Trump securing three of the first four early contests and "Super Tuesday" looming, the debate highlighted a bitter infest among rivals vying to unseat the billionaire real estate mogul for the November election.

Jamala, representing Crimea, won the contest with a song addressing historical events and ethnic cleansing, defeating favorites like Sergey Lazarev and Australia. The victory was seen as a political statement rather than musical quality, sparking controversy over the rules and the ongoing situation in Ukraine. While the result was celebrated by some as a message against current politics, others criticized it as a "political platform," and the UK's Joe and Jake failed to qualify to the top three.

Camber Sands beach in East Sussex will receive £51,000 in new funding for patrols and lifeguard services following the deaths of seven men at the beach last summer. Councillor Sally-Ann Hart emphasized the need for the investment after the incidents were described as "significant and unprecedented," stating that better public education on water safety is essential to prevent future tragedies. The council aims to deploy lifeguards from late May through the summer holidays to protect both visitors and the local tourism economy, while awaiting further inquests into the fatalities.

Osman Partick Thistle manager Osman has expressed concern over the potential departure of assistant manager Archibald, who guided the team to a top-six finish last season. Despite Osman's desire for Archibald to stay, the manager is viewed as one of the best by his players, with midfielder Adam Barton personally disappointed at the prospect of his exit. Meanwhile, Partick Thistle are on the verge of losing centre-back Liam Lindsay, who has traveled to Barnsley for a medical ahead of a likely three-year deal.

Ten individuals were detained at Montreal's Trudeau International Airport after their passports were confiscated. Police stated that no charges have been laid, but investigations are ongoing, and their families have been informed of the situation. The decision to leave the country was made by a single family member, leaving relatives feeling "at a complete loss," while the government commedned the officers' vigilance in protecting communities from global threats.

The 21-year-old made his debut for the Tigers in a League Cup first-round tie against Accrington Stanley in August. Dixon was captain of the Championship club's under-21 side and could make his debut for the Minstermen, who are bottom of the Football League, in Saturday's match against Newport.

An independent report commissioned by the Department of Health estimated that non-European migrants cost the NHS £2 billion annually. Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt stated the government aims to recover money through deterring "health tourism," recovering debts from other countries, and levying non-European temporary residents, insisting the NHS must prioritize care based on "fair contribution" rather than cost. The government has announced a £200 annual levy on migrants from outside the European Economic Area staying between six months and five years to tackle the issue.

Belfast Giants took an early lead through Colin Shields, but Scott Aarssen equalised for the Devils before Ryan Martinelli and Mark Garside restored Glasgow's control in the second period. Belfast extended their advantage with goals from Alex Foster and Steve Saviano, securing a 5-3 victory that leaves the Devils with a game in hand. Cardiff face Blaze on Tuesday while the Giants host Manchester Storm on Wednesday as the festive period continues, with Braehead set to host Coventry on Friday.

After a decade of restoration, a historic steam engine is making its first journey along the East Coast mainline. The locomotive, originally built in Doncaster and named after the Edinburgh to London service, had toured the world as an icon of British engineering before its last class member was withdrawn in 1966.

A judge ruled in favor of one claimant against the Catholic Church, ordering them to pay £14,000 in damages for historical sexual abuse at St William's residential school. However, three other claims were dismissed, and former head James Carragher was jailed for an additional nine years in January 2016. The De La Salle Brothers apologized unreservedly for the abuse, with more compensation claims expected to be heard in late 2017.
